candidate.answerReason: Knowing one line is parallel to the other plane does not determine the containing plane's orientation. Two intersecting planes can contain such a line, so plane parallelism does not follow.

methods.label: Consider the remaining freedom to tilt
methods.explanation: One line only establishes that a line is parallel to a plane. The plane can still tilt about it.
methods.levelReason: The explanation uses elementary spatial reasoning to show why one line is insufficient.

review.mathematicalCheck: Knowing one reference line is parallel to the other plane leaves its containing plane free to rotate about that line. A tilted containing plane can intersect the other plane while the line remains disjoint from it. Therefore plane parallelism does not follow, giving A.
review.levelCheck: The elementary spatial tilting argument is appropriate and sufficient.
review.methodDistinctness: One spatial counterexample argument is enough.
